title: Stabilize allocator prefetch behavior to prevent hosted/dedicated GPU OOM cascades
creator: Nina Patel
description: Customer-reported multi-tenant OOM incidents across Hosted and Dedicated clusters traced to a combination of aggressive prefetching in the runtime allocator and delayed KV cache tombstone reclamation. Symptoms include sudden GPU memory spike followed by OOM kills, session eviction cascades, and corruption-like errors in long-running embeddings/streaming workloads. This ticket tracks the diagnosis, a runtime patch, rollout, and postmortem artifacts.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy model variant X (seq_len 2048) to a mixed-hosted/dedicated pool with enabled prefetch (default runtime config)
2) Start concurrent streaming requests (50-100 qps) from a synthetic workload that uses repeated prefix patterns and long KV lifetimes
3) Observe allocator prefetch memory growth over 30-90s and KV tombstone count increase in per-session index metrics
4) Spike leads to GPU OOM and host process restart; session handles moved and remaining sessions exhibit elevated slab fragmentation and failed KV reads
impact_summary: High-impact: multiple customers experienced application downtime (SLA impact) in both Hosted and Dedicated plans. Private customers with high-concurrency inference also reported similar behavior in air-gapped environments. Affected nodes show >90% GPU memory saturation in ~2 minutes under observed workloads; risk of data loss is low but availability is impacted.
mitigation_and_workaround: 1) Immediate: Disable runtime prefetching via config flag runtime.prefetch.enabled=false for affected pools (applied to Hosted control plane and Dedicated pool rollout)
2) Short-term: Reduce per-session concurrency and lower default batch size to reduce allocator pressure
3) Monitor: Enable kvcache.tombstone_count and allocator.prefetch_bytes alerts, add a temporary rate-limit on long-lived prefix reuse per session
proposed_fix: Introduce a two-part runtime patch: (A) Add adaptive prefetch throttling that measures slab fragmentation and per-GPU free pages, backing off prefetch when fragmentation exceeds threshold; (B) Coalesce KV tombstones more aggressively during high-allocation bursts and force incremental compaction to free handles sooner. Also add a small per-session reservation pool to avoid cross-session stealing in the allocator.
rollout_plan: 1) Create runtime-1.19 candidate with flags: adaptive-prefetch=true, tombstone-coalesce=aggressive, session-reserve=8MB
2) Canary deploy to 5% of hosted nodes and one dedicated pool with low customer impact traffic
3) 48hr soak with detailed telemetry (alloc/gpu/free_pages, kvcache.tombstones, session-evicts)
4) If soak OK, ramp to 25% -> 60% -> 100% across Hosted, then schedule Dedicated/Private upgrades during maintenance windows
5) Post-deploy: keep prefetch off by default for 14 days for new pools and require explicit opt-in after metrics stabilize
testing_plan: Unit: allocator prefetch unit tests for backoff thresholds and reserve accounting
Integration: end-to-end synthetic replay harness with multi-tenant session churn (soak 72h)
Chaos: restart/cgroup pressure tests to ensure graceful fallback and no memory leak across restarts
Regression: run existing KV correctness and embedding accuracy suite to confirm no semantic regressions
comments: 2025-02-10 Nina Patel: Ticket created after escalations from two hosted customers and one dedicated customer. Initial triage shows allocator prefetch and KV tombstone accumulation correlate with incidents.

2025-02-11 Marco Ruiz: Reproduced locally with seq_len=2048 workload. Attaching allocator flame traces and KV tombstone histogram. Initial mitigation (disable prefetch) stopped OOMs in a repro cluster.

2025-02-12 Rahul Desai: Observed atypical slab fragmentation pattern when prefetch requests interleave with async KV writes. Suspect allocator returns aren't compacting contiguous free extents — introduces external fragmentation.
2025-02-13 Design Review (Ana Cho): We should avoid changing public API. Prefetch backoff should be opt-in per pool; add observable signals and a control plane toggle for enterprise customers.
2025-02-14 Marco Ruiz: Branch ready (pr: https://github.com/redwood/realtime-runtime/pull/1284). Patch adds prefetch budget meter and tombstone coalescer. Running CI.
2025-02-16 SRE (Kaitlyn Moore): Deployed hotfix to affected hosted pool and confirmed no new OOMs for 24h. Captured post-hotfix metrics and memory trend graphs in dashboard.
2025-02-18 Customer Success (Liam O'Connor): Notified impacted customers and provided workaround steps. Two customers requested expedited Dedicated upgrades — scheduled maintenance windows.
2025-02-19 Marco Ruiz: Canary started on runtime-1.19-candidate on 5% of hosted; telemetry shows prefetch_bytes dropped by 78% and tombstone compaction rate improved 4x. No regressions so far.
2025-02-20 Nina Patel: Rolling ticket to In Progress for full rollout scope and postmortem write-up. Assigning follow-up ENG-643002 for long-term allocator refactor.
2025-02-20 Marco Ruiz: Added automated alert rules: allocator.prefetch_backoff_count > 5 in 5m and kvcache.tombstone_growth_rate > 100/min trigger P1.
